Durable instance identity is not reserved by the new establishment ledger. Concrete reproduced scenario using real SRD tools on an in-memory database: seed a pre-variant Horn at id horn-of-valhalla#1; adopt_item establishes brass and inserts its permanent trace; remove_item with disposition destroyed deletes the inventory row; give_item for a NEW iron Horn automatically allocates horn-of-valhalla#1 again. The live inventory now says iron while item_variant_establishment still attributes brass to that same instance id. The new table deliberately outlives the inventory row and is keyed only by inventory_id, but itemInstanceIdRetired (packages/core/src/state/itemGrantBinding.ts:228) checks only receipts and effect bindings. This violates the required durable attributable per-instance establishment trace and stable identity/state-integrity boundary (owning dispatch and ADR 0020), even though the newly created physical Horn is distinct. Suggested fix: include item_variant_establishment.inventory_id in the shared retired-id predicate so its durable identity cannot be reissued; preserve the old trace. Sibling search: the same helper governs stateful give_item allocation, explicit-id reassignment, adoption stack splitting, relinquishment allocation and item-state split allocation, so close the shared class rather than special-case Horn grants. Owner: current PR implementation. Required next state: repair and fresh full review at the new exact head before merge. Permanent evidence should be a generalized lifecycle invariant: an establishment record continues to reserve its id after destruction, including automatic allocation and explicit-id reassignment. A compact lifecycle regression is proportionate to durable attribution corruption.
